items.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper addresses the fragility of safety alignment in LLMs, where removing a few key neurons can break safety. Their core method, "Addition by Subtraction," gradually prunes safety-critical neurons during fine-tuning while using preference optimization to re-establish safety through other model components. This approach significantly enhances LLM robustness against pruning-based attacks and other sparsity interventions, making safety alignment less dependent on sparse, vulnerable components.

items.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces "turn-level best-of-N sampling" for LLM agents, using a generator-selector framework. A generator proposes $N$ actions, and a selector chooses the best one at each step. This method significantly improves performance and consistency on complex, long-horizon tasks by enabling off-the-shelf LLMs to directly compare and select actions.

items.title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
items.abstract: This paper introduces ServerBench, a benchmark for coding agents to design specialized LLM serving systems. The core method involves agents experimenting to optimize latency-qualified token value per GPU dollar, with stateful replay and independent verification ensuring correctness. The key contribution is demonstrating that agents, particularly Claude Sonnet 5.5, can significantly outperform existing serving systems by intelligently coordinating capacity and load.

items.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a framework to address the brittleness of LLM social agents, where their behavior changes with minor prompt variations. The core method involves **controlled context enrichment**, systematically adding different types of information to agent prompts to improve their grounding. The main contribution is demonstrating that this enriched context can lead to **selective robustness**, making agents' behavior more stable and predictable under meaning-preserving prompt changes, thereby improving their validation in social simulations.

items.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
items.abstract: This paper argues that current generative AI alignment focuses too narrowly on immediate user satisfaction, neglecting long-term negative impacts on human well-being. It proposes a shift to "long-horizon alignment" that considers how AI shapes human experience over time, mapping trade-offs between short-term utility and long-term costs to foster sustainable human flourishing.

items.title: SecureGARD: Dynamic Ontology-Guided Governance for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.abstract: SecureGARD addresses the security risks of LLM agents executing actions by introducing a dynamic ontology-guided governance framework. It grounds tool calls in a shared semantic representation and uses an executable ontology with task state to make deterministic decisions about tool execution. This allows for bounded replanning when obligations are unmet and enables secure ontology updates, improving generalization and safety across diverse tools.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Motivation for SecureGARD . (a) Interface-specific policies fragment equivalent tool actions. (b) Permission and argument checks cannot verify semantic prerequisites, making binary admission unsafe or overly restrictive. (c) SecureGARD grounds heterogeneous calls into shared actions and checks TBox requirements against verified ABox facts, enabling three-way adjudication and bounded recovery. Three vertically arranged panels illustrate the motivation for SecureGARD. The first shows equivalent email tools with different interfaces, preventing interface-specific policies from transferring. The second shows that permission and argument checks may either allow an unsupported action or block a recoverable task. The third shows SecureGARD grounding heterogeneous tools into a shared semantic action, checking TBox requirements against verified ABox facts, and returning ready, waiting, or forbidden decisions.

items.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
items.abstract: SpecCompact accelerates LLM agent context compaction by generating summary slots in parallel using a small "drafter" model. A larger "verifier" model then semantically checks these slots, allowing for faster processing of long interaction histories. This approach achieves significant speedups while maintaining a balance between information retention and latency.

items.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents
items.abstract: AgentTrustCI is a Java/JUnit 5 framework that tests LLM agents at build-time by expressing security expectations as policy, grounding, and trajectory checks on recorded agent traces. Its core method involves deterministic replay of agent interactions to verify tool usage, answer grounding, and workflow adherence. The contribution is a robust testing pipeline that accurately identifies security faults and ensures LLM agents operate reliably and securely within defined constraints.

items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.abstract: This paper introduces CompressionBench, a framework for evaluating coding agents' ability to autonomously compress Large Language Models (LLMs). The core method involves agents receiving a source LLM and constraints, then developing their own compression algorithms to produce smaller, functional models. The contribution is demonstrating that coding agents can effectively perform LLM compression, achieving competitive performance with significantly reduced model sizes, and providing insights into their strategies.

items.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
items.abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of dexterous robotic hands in the context of foundation models, organizing research across hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, learning, and evaluation. Its core contribution lies in connecting these interdependent layers and highlighting that the effectiveness of human data for robotic learning hinges on kinematic, visual, and contact alignment, not just sheer volume.

items.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
items.abstract: This paper introduces EmoReward, a novel self-evolving reward calibration method for emotional video generation. It addresses the challenge of subjective video quality evaluation by adaptively adjusting reward weights based on the reliability of evidence observed during training. EmoReward's core contribution is its ability to dynamically learn which emotional cues are most trustworthy and how to best weight them, leading to more effective and robust emotional video generation.

items.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
items.abstract: This paper introduces Cosmos, a framework for real-time interactive world simulation for Physical AI. It adapts foundation models to stream visual observations based on actions and scene controls, allowing users and agents to interact with dynamic virtual environments. The core contribution is enabling both predicting action consequences and generating observations from external simulators, facilitating training and evaluation in interactive virtual settings.

items.title: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks
items.abstract: LifeVal is a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI models on personalized, agentic consumer tasks. It focuses on high-value life activities that a digital assistant could automate, drawing on extensive consumer surveys to quantify their economic importance. The benchmark's unique contribution lies in its personalized task creation, using real user data like chat histories and personal files to create realistic evaluation scenarios.
items.figure_caption: Example LifeVal Tasks. Any personal information in the paper, including any images with personal information, has been deidentified or synthetically generated to protect our task creators’ privacy.

items.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
items.abstract: This paper introduces RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework for edge resource management that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Generative AI (Gen-AI). Its core method uses a Multi-Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) enhanced by a Large Language Model (LLM) for reward generalization, addressing a key challenge in complex RL workflows. The main contribution is an agentic approach that optimizes resource allocation at Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units by interpreting system states and evaluating trade-offs, with the LLM providing crucial feedback for improved decision-making.

items.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces
items.abstract: This paper introduces ZETA, a novel architecture for vision agents that separates the decision-making process (routing policy) from the execution of visual tools. This decoupling allows the agent to first determine the correct scientific reasoning and then invoke specialized tools for execution, improving auditability and reliability. ZETA's core contribution is enabling scientific vision agents to be more trustworthy by clearly distinguishing between reasoning errors and execution failures.
items.figure_caption: Effect of constrained action space v routing policy specification

items.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
items.abstract: This paper introduces Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD) to improve reinforcement learning by using natural language "process rubrics" derived from agent trajectories. ORSD generates these rubrics dynamically, distilling behavioral differences into dense, token-level supervision signals. This allows the agent to learn from both successful and failed attempts within a trajectory, leading to more effective credit assignment than traditional sparse reward methods.
items.figure_caption: The overview of ORSD. (a) For each task, the policy first samples a group of trajectories. It then takes the task description and these trajectories as inputs to generate multiple rubric bundles. (b) Each Rubric bundle is evaluated on every trajectory, the rubric bundle with the largest rubric-reward alignment score is selected. (c) The selected rubric bundle is used to augment the context and compute the per-token likelihood gap between augmented and non-augmented contexts, enabling per-token advantage shaping of the original trajectory-level advantage.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether generalist robot policies can be improved across multiple tasks simultaneously using reinforcement learning (RL) in a deployment setting. The core method involves developing structured evaluations to test this multi-task improvement capability and identifying the optimal algorithmic approach. The contribution is demonstrating that generalist policies can indeed scale their performance across diverse tasks through iterated RL, paving the way for more adaptable and capable robots.

items.title: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Test-Time Reasoning with Imperfect Generators and Verifiers
items.abstract: This paper introduces Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency (VGSC), a novel decoding framework for improving multi-step reasoning in large language models. VGSC balances the generator's diversity with the verifier's correctness by using step-level correctness and future-outcome estimates to guide generation. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of existing methods that either favor diversity or can amplify verifier errors, leading to more robust and accurate reasoning at test time.

items.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
items.abstract: Paper: summary generation failed.
items.figure_caption: Overview of Visual Token Routing (VTR). Spatio-temporal router: A lightweight router reads each image region across the current and previous screenshots and decides whether its visual token enters the language model. Zoomed-in region: While the agent types a file name into a save dialog in front of a playing video, the router keeps only the tokens of the typed file name. It drops the regions that did not change, and also drops the circled part of the video, which changed but is not relevant to the task.

items.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
items.abstract: This paper diagnoses failures in a vision-language agent playing Pac-Man by separating perception and decision-making. Their core method involves using textual board representations to isolate policy improvements and conducting specific perception checks. The key contribution is demonstrating that perception can be accurate statically but fail during interaction, and that policy optimization doesn't always equate to better action choices, highlighting the need for nuanced post-training evaluation.

EmoReward's core contribution is its ability to dynamically learn which emotional cues are most trustworthy and how to best weight them, leading to more effective and robust emotional video generation.

papers.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Cosmos, a framework for real-time interactive world simulation for Physical AI. It adapts foundation models to stream visual observations based on actions and scene controls, allowing users and agents to interact with dynamic virtual environments. The core contribution is enabling both predicting action consequences and generating observations from external simulators, facilitating training and evaluation in interactive virtual settings.

papers.title: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks
papers.abstract: LifeVal is a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI models on personalized, agentic consumer tasks. It focuses on high-value life activities that a digital assistant could automate, drawing on extensive consumer surveys to quantify their economic importance. The benchmark's unique contribution lies in its personalized task creation, using real user data like chat histories and personal files to create realistic evaluation scenarios.
papers.figure_caption: Example LifeVal Tasks. Any personal information in the paper, including any images with personal information, has been deidentified or synthetically generated to protect our task creators’ privacy.

papers.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
papers.abstract: This paper introduces RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework for edge resource management that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Generative AI (Gen-AI). Its core method uses a Multi-Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) enhanced by a Large Language Model (LLM) for reward generalization, addressing a key challenge in complex RL workflows. The main contribution is an agentic approach that optimizes resource allocation at Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units by interpreting system states and evaluating trade-offs, with the LLM providing crucial feedback for improved decision-making.

papers.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ZETA, a novel architecture for vision agents that separates the decision-making process (routing policy) from the execution of visual tools. This decoupling allows the agent to first determine the correct scientific reasoning and then invoke specialized tools for execution, improving auditability and reliability. ZETA's core contribution is enabling scientific vision agents to be more trustworthy by clearly distinguishing between reasoning errors and execution failures.
papers.figure_caption: Effect of constrained action space v routing policy specification

papers.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD) to improve reinforcement learning by using natural language "process rubrics" derived from agent trajectories. ORSD generates these rubrics dynamically, distilling behavioral differences into dense, token-level supervision signals. This allows the agent to learn from both successful and failed attempts within a trajectory, leading to more effective credit assignment than traditional sparse reward methods.
papers.figure_caption: The overview of ORSD. (a) For each task, the policy first samples a group of trajectories. It then takes the task description and these trajectories as inputs to generate multiple rubric bundles. (b) Each Rubric bundle is evaluated on every trajectory, the rubric bundle with the largest rubric-reward alignment score is selected. (c) The selected rubric bundle is used to augment the context and compute the per-token likelihood gap between augmented and non-augmented contexts, enabling per-token advantage shaping of the original trajectory-level advantage.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether generalist robot policies can be improved across multiple tasks simultaneously using reinforcement learning (RL) in a deployment setting. The core method involves developing structured evaluations to test this multi-task improvement capability and identifying the optimal algorithmic approach. The contribution is demonstrating that generalist policies can indeed scale their performance across diverse tasks through iterated RL, paving the way for more adaptable and capable robots.

papers.title: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Test-Time Reasoning with Imperfect Generators and Verifiers
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency (VGSC), a novel decoding framework for improving multi-step reasoning in large language models. VGSC balances the generator's diversity with the verifier's correctness by using step-level correctness and future-outcome estimates to guide generation. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of existing methods that either favor diversity or can amplify verifier errors, leading to more robust and accurate reasoning at test time.

papers.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
papers.abstract: Paper: summary generation failed.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of Visual Token Routing (VTR). Spatio-temporal router: A lightweight router reads each image region across the current and previous screenshots and decides whether its visual token enters the language model. Zoomed-in region: While the agent types a file name into a save dialog in front of a playing video, the router keeps only the tokens of the typed file name. It drops the regions that did not change, and also drops the circled part of the video, which changed but is not relevant to the task.

papers.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
papers.abstract: This paper diagnoses failures in a vision-language agent playing Pac-Man by separating perception and decision-making. Their core method involves using textual board representations to isolate policy improvements and conducting specific perception checks. The key contribution is demonstrating that perception can be accurate statically but fail during interaction, and that policy optimization doesn't always equate to better action choices, highlighting the need for nuanced post-training evaluation.
